To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) physiological signals monitored by sensors are correlated with affective states of a user in an HCI environment, and (b) the pupil diameter is the most significant indicator for stress detection in HCI.
the physiological signals (BVP, GSR, PD and ST) are correlated to the affective states of computer users.
the physiological signals of GSR, BVP, PD and ST can be used to recognize the affective state of a computer user.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an emotion recognition system that is capable of monitoring and analyzing the physiological signals of computer users to detect their stress levels.
the development of a system that is capable of recognizing stress in computer users based on the analysis of physiological signals.
the development of an affective computing system that is able to detect stress in computer users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed system is capable of recognizing the affective state of computer users based on the physiological responses of the body.
stress detection in computer users is feasible and that the physiological signals can be used to detect affective states of the users.
the physiological signals used in this research can be effectively used for the recognition of stress in computer users.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the physiological signals can be used for affective recognition and the proposed system can be used as an early warning system to prevent stress related injuries.
the physiological signals of the human body are indeed sensitive to the changes in the emotional state and that these signals can be used to detect stress in a computer user.

the stress recognition system developed is able to detect the affective state of the computer user with an overall accuracy of 90% and the pupil diameter is the most important affective state indicator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the physiological sensing of the computer user can be used for affective recognition.
the physiological signals of a computer user do, in fact change when the user's affective state changes.
the affective states of a user in a computer-based interaction environment can indeed be detected by monitoring the physiological changes in the user.
